title: Great Pyramid of Giza completed
description: Conventional Egyptological estimate for completion of the Great Pyramid, tomb of Pharaoh Khufu; exact year is not precisely known.

title: Code of Hammurabi promulgated
description: One of the earliest and best-preserved written legal codes, issued by the Babylonian king Hammurabi.

title: Traditional founding of Rome
description: Legendary date (April 21, 753 BCE) traditionally ascribed to Rome's founding by Romulus; not a historically verified event.

title: Battle of Marathon
description: Athenian-led Greek forces defeated the first Persian invasion of Greece under Darius I.

title: Archimedes' principle of buoyancy
description: Archimedes formulates the principle relating buoyant force to displaced fluid weight.

title: Birth of Confucius
description: Traditional birth date of the Chinese philosopher whose teachings shaped East Asian ethics and governance for millennia.

title: Enlightenment of the Buddha
description: Traditional (though disputed) date for Siddhartha Gautama's enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, founding event of Buddhism.

title: Death of Alexander the Great
description: Death of Alexander III of Macedon in Babylon, precipitating the breakup of his empire among the Diadochi.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
description: Julius Caesar was stabbed to death by a group of senators, including Brutus and Cassius, on the Ides of March.

title: Eruption of Vesuvius destroys Pompeii
description: Mount Vesuvius erupted, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash; the traditional August date is disputed by some modern scholars in favor of an autumn eruption.

wiki.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

title: Ptolemy compiles the Almagest
description: Claudius Ptolemy's geocentric astronomical treatise, the authoritative model of the cosmos in Europe and the Islamic world for over a millennium.

title: Cai Lun refines papermaking
description: Traditional date for Cai Lun's improved papermaking process, reported to the Han imperial court.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Deposition of Romulus Augustulus by Odoacer, conventionally marking the end of the Western Roman Empire.

wiki.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

title: Hijra: Muhammad's migration to Medina
description: Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Medina, an event marking year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

title: Battle of Hastings
description: William, Duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold II, beginning the Norman conquest of England.

title: Magna Carta sealed
description: King John sealed the Magna Carta, limiting royal authority and establishing early principles of due process.

title: Black Death reaches Europe
description: Plague-carrying ships arrived in Messina, marking the start of the Black Death's spread across Europe, which killed an estimated third of the population.

title: Gutenberg's printing press
description: Johannes Gutenberg developed the movable-type printing press in Mainz, transforming the spread of written knowledge in Europe.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: Ottoman forces under Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

title: Columbus reaches the Americas
description: Christopher Columbus's expedition made landfall in the Bahamas, beginning sustained European contact with the Americas.

title: Copernicus publishes De revolutionibus
description: Nicolaus Copernicus's treatise proposing a heliocentric model of the solar system was published near his death.

title: Luther's Ninety-Five Theses
description: Martin Luther's traditional posting of the Ninety-Five Theses in Wittenberg, a catalyst for the Protestant Reformation.

title: Galileo's telescopic observations
description: Galileo Galilei's telescopic observations of the Moon, Jupiter's moons, and the phases of Venus provided strong support for heliocentrism.

title: Newton publishes the Principia
description: Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica established the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

title: US Declaration of Independence
description: The Second Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence, formally announcing separation from Great Britain.

title: Storming of the Bastille
description: Parisian revolutionaries stormed the Bastille fortress, a defining event of the French Revolution.

title: Priestley isolates oxygen
description: Joseph Priestley isolated and identified oxygen gas, independently of Carl Wilhelm Scheele's earlier work.

title: Premiere of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony
description: Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, featuring the 'Ode to Joy,' premiered in Vienna while the composer was almost completely deaf.

title: Earliest surviving photograph
description: Nicéphore Niépce produced 'View from the Window at Le Gras,' the oldest surviving photograph made in a camera.

wiki.title: View from the Window at Le Gras

title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
description: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species introduced the theory of evolution by natural selection.

title: Battle of Waterloo
description: A coalition led by the Duke of Wellington and Gebhard von Blücher defeated Napoleon, ending his rule as Emperor of the French.

title: Emancipation Proclamation takes effect
description: President Abraham Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation declared enslaved people in Confederate states to be free.

title: Röntgen discovers X-rays
description: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered a new form of electromagnetic radiation, which he called X-rays, earning the first Nobel Prize in Physics.

title: First public film screening
description: The Lumière brothers held the first commercial public screening of projected motion pictures at the Grand Café in Paris.

title: First powered flight
description: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the first sustained, controlled, powered flight of a heavier-than-air aircraft.

title: Einstein's special relativity
description: Albert Einstein published 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies,' introducing special relativity.

title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
description: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria triggered the July Crisis leading to World War I.

title: Einstein's general relativity
description: Albert Einstein presented the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

title: Armistice ends World War I
description: The Armistice of 11 November 1918 ended fighting on the Western Front, effectively concluding World War I.

title: Fleming discovers penicillin
description: Alexander Fleming noticed a mold, Penicillium, killing bacteria in a petri dish, leading to the development of the first antibiotic.

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
description: Japan's surprise attack on the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor brought the United States into World War II.

title: First self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction
description: Enrico Fermi's team achieved the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction beneath the University of Chicago's Stagg Field.

title: D-Day landings in Normandy
description: Allied forces launched the largest seaborne invasion in history, opening the Western Front against Nazi Germany.

title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
description: The United States dropped the first atomic bomb used in war on Hiroshima, killing tens of thousands and hastening Japan's surrender.

wiki.title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

title: Japan formally surrenders, ending World War II
description: Japan's formal surrender aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay ended the Second World War.

title: Watson and Crick describe DNA's double helix
description: James Watson and Francis Crick, building on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, published the double-helix structure of DNA in Nature.

title: First human spaceflight (Yuri Gagarin)
description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human to journey into outer space aboard Vostok 1.

title: Apollo 11 Moon landing

place.region: Kennedy Space Center, USA (launch site; landing on the Moon)

description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon; the mission launched from Kennedy Space Center.

title: Invention of the World Wide Web
description: Tim Berners-Lee submitted his proposal for an information management system at CERN, the origin of the World Wide Web.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: East German authorities opened the border crossings, and jubilant crowds began dismantling the Berlin Wall, symbolizing the end of the Cold War divide.

title: Human Genome Project completed
description: The international Human Genome Project announced completion of a essentially full sequence of the human genome.

title: September 11 attacks
description: Coordinated terrorist attacks destroyed the World Trade Center towers and struck the Pentagon, killing nearly 3,000 people.

title: First direct detection of gravitational waves
description: The LIGO observatories directly detected gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger, confirming a key prediction of general relativity.

title: First image of a black hole
description: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first-ever direct image of a black hole's silhouette, at the center of galaxy M87.
